subproblem.title: The open unit cube in Euclid k has Lebesgue measure 1
subproblem.statement: For every k ∈ ℕ, the open unit cube Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i ∈ Fin k} in Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) has Lebesgue measure volume(Q₁) = 1 (as an element of [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ k : ℕ, volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the notation paragraph of the parent proof ('Under the measure-preserving linear isometry Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) ... Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ), so ... vol(Q₁) = 1'). Here it is specialized to δ = 0 and stated for every dimension k.

Let k ∈ ℕ and Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i ∈ Fin k}. Here y_i = y i is the i-th coordinate, i.e. the i-th component of WithLp.ofLp y ∈ (Fin k → ℝ).

1. Let B := ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} (0, 1) = Set.univ.pi (fun _ => Set.Ioo 0 1) ⊆ (Fin k → ℝ). B is measurable because it is a finite product of open intervals (MeasurableSet.univ_pi, measurableSet_Ioo). In particular it is null-measurable.
2. The coordinate map ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is measure preserving, from the volume (Lebesgue measure) of Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) to the product Lebesgue measure on Fin k → ℝ (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin k); equivalently EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp).
3. Q₁ = ofLp⁻¹(B). For y ∈ Euclid k: y ∈ Q₁ ⟺ ∀ i, 0 < (ofLp y) i ∧ (ofLp y) i < 1 ⟺ ∀ i, (ofLp y) i ∈ Ioo 0 1 ⟺ ofLp y ∈ B (Set.mem_pi; in Lean, ext y; simp [Set.mem_pi]).
4. Applying step 2 to the null-measurable set B (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage) gives volume(Q₁) = volume(ofLp⁻¹(B)) = volume(B).
5. By the product formula for open boxes (Real.volume_pi_Ioo), volume(B) = ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} ENNReal.ofReal(1 − 0) = ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} 1 = 1. When k = 0 this is the empty product, which is also 1.
6. By steps 4 and 5, volume(Q₁) = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Q₁ is the preimage of the box B = ∏_i (0,1) under the coordinate map ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ).
ofLp is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), so vol(Q₁) = vol(B) because B is measurable.
vol(B) = ∏_i ofReal(1 − 0) = 1 by Real.volume_pi_Ioo (the empty product when k = 0).

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree for every natural dimension. The measurable product box is precisely the coordinate-map preimage defining the cube. Volume preservation and the open-box product formula prove the conclusion, including the empty product when k = 0. This independently supplies the parent's probability normalization.
